Route 7[edit]

Route 7 is a short path that links Saffron City to the east and Celadon City to the west. The western end of the second Underground Path emerges here, but authorities have closed the tunnel indefinitely because of rowdy Trainers battling inside.

Celadon City[edit]

Celadon City is located between Route 7 to the east and Route 16 to the west. The Celadon Department Store in the northwest offers all kinds of items for sale, and the Celadon Condominiums acts as a hotel. Visitors can try their luck at the Game Corner in the heart of the city and redeem their winnings at the Prize Corner next door. The Celadon Gym stands on a hill in the southwest part of town.

Celadon Condominiums[edit]

3F[edit]

Enter the Celadon Condominiums building and enter the elevator on 1F. Climb to 3F to visit the Game Freak Development Room. When you step out of the elevator, Lyra/Ethan and Marill rush over to greet you. She/He excitedly tells you that the Sound Designer just showed her/him a cool device, a high-tech machine that plays retro music originally from the Game Boy. The designer is apparently hoping to give the device to someone who has won all of the Kanto Badges. Lyra/Ethan suggests that you go for it, then hurries off. The Sound Designer can be found standing near the large globe in the corner. Speak to him after obtaining all 16 Badges, and he rewards you with the GB Sounds.

Rooftop[edit]

After the sun sets, enter the Celadon Condominiums building and climb the stairs to 2F. There are two elevators here. The left-hand elevator is inaccessible from here, and leads between 1F, 3F, and the roof. Take the right-hand elevator instead to reach the rooftop's inner area. Speak to the man in the exterior room to hear a scary story, and receive a Spell Tag for listening to the entire thing.

Restaurant[edit]

The restaurant on the south side of town is currently hosting an eat-a-thon. It seems as though Maylene is no pushover!

Game Corner[edit]

The prizes offered next door are expensive, so it will require a large number of coins to receive all of them. Like the one in Goldenrod City, the Celadon Game Corner features only the Voltorb Flip card game.

A Hidden Power[edit]

Speak to the Guitarist standing next to the counter, and he mentions how his secret skill allows him to identify a Pokémon's hidden power. The move Hidden Power changes its type based on an individual Pokémon's attributes, which can give the user a valuable way to cover its weaknesses. Show the man a Pokémon, and he reveals the type that Hidden Power would take if used by the Pokémon.

The Masked Man[edit]

A masked man can be seen standing near the counter on 2F. Speak to him, and he assumes that you want his Crasher Wake mask, and adamantly refuses to ever let it go. He then realizes that you were more interested in the other mask that he was examining, and gives you the Turtwig Mask Accessory instead. The man eventually gives you a Chimchar Mask and Piplup Mask, as well. He has already paid for them, and gives them as a gift from "the one who wears masks the best".

Celadon Gym[edit]

Celadon City Pokémon Gym
Leader: Erika
The Nature-Loving Princess


The Celadon Gym specializes in Grass-type Pokémon. Grass-type moves are super effective against Ground-, Rock-, and Water-type Pokémon, while Grass-type Pokémon are weak to Bug-, Fire-, Flying-, Ice-, and Poison-type moves.

The Gym is designed as a greenhouse, with many flower arrangements on display. Use Cut to clear a path and pass under the first archway. Turn left, pass by Twins Jo & Zoe, then move in a clockwise "C" direction. Loop around the flowerbed in the middle of the Gym to pass under the archway in the southeast corner, then go north. Continue on past Picnicker Tanya, then turn west. Pass by Beauty Julia and walk under the middle and western archways. Use Cut a second and third time to remove two more small trees to reach the Gym Leader.

Erika leads with her Jumpluff. Both Leech Seed and Giga Drain steal the target's HP, and Sunny Day triggers its Chlorophyll Ability to boost its already-high Speed. As a Grass/Flying Pokémon, it takes massive damage from Ice-type attacks. Her Tangela can further harass its target with Sleep Powder, and AncientPower lets it fight back against the Grass type's common counters: Fire, Ice, Bug, and Flying Pokémon. Victreebel's Leaf Storm is powerful, but cuts its Special Attack with every use. As plants rely on the sun for nutrients, Erika's remaining two Pokémon rely on Sunny Day to prepare their combination moves. Victreebel regains more HP than normal under harsh sunlight with Synthesis, and Bellossom does the same. Under these conditions, Bellossom can launch its strongest move, SolarBeam, without first taking a turn to charge it.
